title: Event bus class design
idea: The event bus class design gives `EventBus` named topics; a `Publisher` sends an `Event` to one topic, and each `Subscription` there hands it to one `Subscriber`.

analogy.text: A building has one noticeboard per subject. Pinning a notice copies it into the pigeonhole of everyone who signed up for that board.
analogy.breaks: No copies are made: every subscriber gets the same immutable event.

points: `Event` is an immutable record: id, topic, key and payload.
`Topic` owns its subscriptions; `EventBus` maps names to topics.
`Subscription` pairs one `Subscriber` with a filter that picks its events.
`Publisher` is bound to one topic, so callers cannot misroute events.

edges.label: uses
edges.caption: A publisher holds one topic name and forwards each publish call to the bus.

edges.label: creates
edges.caption: The bus assigns the event id, so ids are unique across publishers.

edges.label: has many
edges.caption: The bus keeps topics by name and refuses names it does not know.

edges.label: has many
edges.caption: A topic holds zero or more subscriptions. Removing one leaves the others untouched.

edges.label: has 1
edges.caption: The filter decides whether this subscriber wants an event at all.

edges.label: has 1
edges.caption: Each subscription points to exactly one handler.

edges.label: is-a
edges.caption: Concrete handlers implement Subscriber. The bus never knows their class.

code.title: Model and a short demo
code.caption: The whole model in one file, with synchronous delivery for now. Retries and a mailbox arrive on the next page.

walk.text: Create the topic, then a publisher bound to it.
Email takes every event; refunds filters to cancellations only.
After unsubscribe, the refunds handler no longer receives events.
Asking for an unknown topic fails fast with a clear message.
Event is an immutable record; Subscriber is a two-method contract.
Topic owns its subscriptions and hands out a copy to iterate.
Publish assigns an id, then delivers to each matching subscription.

pitfalls: Do not let subscribers see the bus internals; give them only the event.
Return a `Subscription` handle from subscribe, so unsubscribe removes exactly that one.
Make `Event` immutable; one shared copy reaches many subscribers.

quiz.q: Which line does ClassDesign print for EV-3?
options: Both email and refunds receive EV-3
quiz.why: Refunds was unsubscribed before EV-3 was published, so only the email subscription remains on the topic to receive it.

takeaway: Topics own subscriptions; each subscription joins one filter to one subscriber.

starters: Why is Publisher bound to a single topic?
Should the filter live on the subscription or the subscriber?
How would wildcard topics like orders.* change this design?
